input.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, narrow Customer's indemnity, and add indemnity procedure, exclusions and Section 20.5 infringement remedies
input.comment: [Playbook] We added the Vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breaches and wilful misconduct, and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law, per our playbook position. We also added the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, the usual IP exclusions and the Section 20.5 procure-modify-replace-refund remedies that Section 9.3 already cross-references.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. 20.2 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of content or materials Customer provides to Vendor or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. 20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim; the indemnifying Party shall control the defence and settlement, provided it may not settle in a way that imposes a non-monetary obligation or admission on the indemnified Party without its consent; and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate with its own counsel at its own cost. 20.4 Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or Deliverables, their combination with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications. 20.5 For a claim under Section 20.1(a), Vendor shall at its expense procure the rights necessary for Customer's continued use, or modify or replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item; if neither is commercially practicable, Customer may terminate the affected Services and receive a refund of Fees paid for the affected item allocable to the unused period.
